title: ReviewPlane browser-worker protocol, version 1
description: Single source for the version 1 browser-worker protocol: the mutually authenticated internal channel between the control-plane server and a central Chromium worker (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.5, 6.4 and 11). TypeScript models, validators and canonical encoders are generated from this file. Hand-maintained equivalents in apps/server or apps/browser-worker are a review failure.

channels.control: Worker identity, assignment and browser-session lifecycle.

worker.register.description: Worker announces its identity, browser build, capacity and sandbox posture (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, docs/SECURITY.md section 6.4).

worker.register.ack.description: Control plane assigns the worker identity and the projects the worker may accept sessions for (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.4).

worker.heartbeat.description: Periodic capacity and liveness report used to detect a crashed or orphaned worker (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 14).

worker.heartbeat.ack.description: Answer to a heartbeat, restating the worker's current project assignment. Restating it on every heartbeat is what bounds the staleness of a revocation to one heartbeat interval: an assignment learned only at registration would let an unassigned project keep working until the worker restarted (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.4, ADR-0026).

worker.contexts.request.description: Asks the worker to enumerate the browser contexts it is actually holding, for the reconciliation of docs/OPERATIONS.md section 9.

worker.contexts.description: The browser contexts the worker holds. Reconciliation compares this against control-plane state and terminates the contexts no live session claims (docs/OPERATIONS.md section 9).

browser_session.allocate.description: Instruction to allocate an isolated browser context with an ephemeral profile for one browser session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 12, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.2).

browser_session.allocated.description: Worker reports the allocated context, browser build and initial control epoch.

browser_session.status.description: Worker-observed lifecycle transition of a browser session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 12, docs/EVENTS.md section 7).

browser_session.terminate.description: Instruction to close the context and destroy its ephemeral session data (docs/SECURITY.md section 10).

browser.command.description: One browser command. The envelope carries the browser session, controller identity, control epoch, sequence number and timestamp required by docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4.

browser.command.result.description: Result of one browser command. Any page-derived content is labelled untrusted (ADR-0010, docs/SECURITY.md section 11).

frame_too_large.description: The encoded frame exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The frame was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_protocol_version.description: protocol_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts.

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not a version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored.

payload_too_large.description: The payload exceeded the byte bound declared for its message type. Snapshot and screenshot results are bounded here as well as by the worker, per docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13.

schema_violation.description: The frame parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its message type.

interactive_commands.description: Commands that operate the page on behalf of a controller. They require the issuing controller to hold the current interactive control lease (docs/SECURITY.md section 7, ADR-0007).

system_capture_commands.description: Non-interactive capture commands. A system controller may issue these without holding the interactive lease, and doing so never transfers or revokes it (docs/TESTING.md section 5).

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

build_version.description: Worker or browser build version, for example 0.1.0 or 143.0.7499.4.

worker_label.description: Scheduling label advertised by the worker build (docs/CONFIGURATION.md section 3).

origin.description: Absolute origin of the published development service the session may reach, for example https://public-alias.internal.invalid (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.3). The leftmost label is the published service's public_alias, never its svc_ identifier, which is not a valid DNS label. Egress beyond this origin is refused by the worker.

session_capability.description: Session-scoped route capability (docs/SECURITY.md section 9). Sensitive: it is a bearer credential and is redacted in log, debug and default JSON representations. It is the same credential the connector protocol carries under this name, so one failure to redact cannot exist on only one of the two paths.

navigation_target.description: Absolute URL or root-relative path. A relative path is resolved against the published service origin of the session (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4).

resolved_url.description: Absolute URL observed by the browser. Page-derived, so bounded in length and character class only.

page_text.description: Short page-derived text such as a document title. Untrusted content (ADR-0010): control characters are excluded and the length is bounded so that a hostile page cannot inflate a response.

snapshot_text.description: Rendered accessibility snapshot in the indented form of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4. Untrusted content: bounded, newline-separated, and never interpreted as an instruction.

element_reference.description: Reference to one element of a single snapshot. References are valid only for the snapshot that produced them and are invalidated by a resize (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4).

accessible_role.description: Accessibility role of a snapshot element. Page-derived and bounded.

input_text.description: Text typed into a page input. Secret values MUST NOT travel through this field; docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.9 secret injection is the supported path.

option_value.description: Value of one option of a select. Page-derived in practice, so bounded in length and character class.

selector.description: CSS selector used by a bounded wait condition. Selectors are hints, not identity (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 17).

url_pattern.description: Substring a URL must contain for a url_matches wait condition to be satisfied.

reason_text.description: Short operator-facing explanation. Never carries page content verbatim beyond its bound, and never carries credentials (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

sha256_hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of an artefact's bytes, verified server-side before the artefact becomes available (docs/API.md section 15, ADR-0012).

message_type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected, never ignored. This enumeration MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages.

error_class.description: Stable error class. The browser-worker channel reuses the docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12 codes so that a refusal reaches the agent unchanged, plus PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED for a frame this build cannot parse. This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes.

controller_type.description: Kind of controller holding or requesting browser control (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 13). Stage 0 issues leases to agent and system controllers only; human is present because ADR-0007 fixes the vocabulary.

termination_reason.description: Why a browser session is being terminated.

browser_type.description: Browser engine. ADR-0001 fixes Chromium for the initial architecture.

retention_class.description: Retention class applied to evidence captured in this session (docs/SECURITY.md section 14).

command_name.description: Browser command. Membership of x-protocol.vocabularies.interactive_commands decides whether the issuing controller must hold the interactive lease.

key_name.description: A key press, optionally with modifiers. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: a key name reaches the browser as a control instruction, so it is drawn from a fixed set rather than passed through from an argument a page could influence.

wait_until.description: Bounded navigation wait condition (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4). Every value completes or times out; none waits indefinitely.

wait_condition.description: Bounded wait condition. docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 forbids an unbounded sleep, so every condition is paired with a timeout.

screenshot_purpose.description: Why a screenshot is being captured. system is the non-interactive capture that never takes the interactive lease.

image_content_type.description: Media type of a captured screenshot. PNG only, so the original evidence is lossless (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 20).

trust_label.description: Trust of the content in a result (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 6). A result carrying page-derived content MUST declare untrusted_browser_content; the schema refuses the alternative.

instruction_policy.description: How the receiver must treat content in this result. The single value is deliberate: nothing a browser worker returns is ever an instruction (ADR-0010, docs/SECURITY.md section 11).

envelope.description: Browser-worker message envelope. The command fields of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4 — browser session, controller identity, control epoch, sequence and timestamp — live here rather than in each payload, so no command can omit them.

protocol_version.description: Protocol version. Stage 0 accepts 1 only; any other value is rejected with PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED and is never best-effort parsed.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned message identifier, conventionally prefixed msg_.

type.description: Version 1 message type. Unknown types are rejected.

sent_at.description: Time the sender emitted the message. Required on every message by docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4.

worker_id.description: Worker identity, conventionally prefixed wkr_. Absent on worker.register, where the identity is still being established, and required on every other message.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the message concerns, conventionally prefixed brs_.

controller.description: Controller on whose behalf a command is issued.

control_epoch.description: Control epoch the sender believes is current. A command carrying a prior epoch is rejected with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE (ADR-0007).

sequence.description: Monotonically increasing per-session command sequence, used for replay detection and ordering (docs/SECURITY.md section 8).

correlation_id.description: Identifier of the message this message answers.

payload.description: Message payload. Its schema is selected by type. The frame is bounded by x-protocol.limits.max_control_frame_bytes and each payload by its own x-max-bytes.

x-requires.detail: registration precedes worker identity assignment
every message after registration is attributed to a worker identity
session-scoped messages name their browser session
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4 requires controller identity, control epoch and sequence on every browser command
a result names the command it answers

controller_identity.description: Identity of the controller issuing a command (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 13, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4).

id.description: Opaque controller identity, for example an agent session identifier.

viewport.description: Browser viewport in CSS pixels plus device pixel ratio (docs/API.md section 11). The required presets are 1440x900 and 390x844 (AGENTS.md Browser-facing work).

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio. A screenshot is device_scale_factor times the CSS viewport in each dimension, which annotation geometry depends on (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16).

session_limits.description: Limits the worker enforces itself, so a session cannot outlive or outgrow its allocation even if the control plane is unreachable (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.5, docs/CONFIGURATION.md section 3).

max_duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock lifetime of the session. The worker terminates the context when it elapses.

default_timeout_ms.description: Timeout applied to a command that does not state one.

max_command_timeout_ms.description: Upper bound on any command timeout, so no command can wait indefinitely.

screenshot_max_bytes.description: Largest screenshot the worker will upload.

snapshot_max_nodes.description: Largest number of elements a snapshot may describe before it is truncated.

snapshot_max_bytes.description: Largest rendered snapshot the worker will return before truncation (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13).

worker_registration.description: Worker self-description presented when it registers.

browser_version.description: Browser build version, recorded on every browser session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 12).

capacity.description: Concurrent browser sessions this worker accepts. Exceeding it is refused with BROWSER_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED.

labels.description: Scheduling labels. Stage 0 has a single worker and does not schedule by label.

sandbox_enabled.description: Whether the Chromium sandbox is enabled. docs/SECURITY.md section 10 requires it; a worker reporting false is a high-risk configuration the control plane records and refuses in Stage 0.

worker_registration_ack.description: Assigns the worker identity and the projects it may serve.

accepted.description: Whether the control plane accepted the worker.

assigned_projects.description: Projects this worker may accept sessions for. A session for any other project is refused with PROJECT_CONTEXT_MISMATCH (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.4).

session_limits.description: Default limits applied to sessions allocated to this worker.

heartbeat_interval_seconds.description: How often the worker must heartbeat before the control plane treats it as lost.

active_sessions.description: Browser sessions currently allocated on this worker.

capacity.description: Concurrent browser sessions this worker accepts.

resident_memory_mb.description: Resident memory of the worker process tree, for capacity diagnosis.

worker_heartbeat_ack.description: Answer to a heartbeat. It restates the assignment rather than describing a change, so a worker that missed an earlier answer converges anyway and no side has to keep a diff (ADR-0026).

assigned_projects.description: The complete set of projects this worker may accept sessions for, as of this answer. An assignment removed here MUST stop being served without waiting for a restart (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.4).

heartbeat_interval_seconds.description: How often the worker must heartbeat before the control plane treats it as lost. Repeated here so an operator can change the cadence without restarting the worker.

observed_at.description: When the control plane read the assignment.

worker_contexts_request.description: Asks the worker what it is holding. It takes no arguments: a reconciler that could name the sessions it expects would be told what it already believes.

worker_context.description: One browser context the worker is holding.

browser_session_id.description: Browser session the context was allocated for.

status.description: Status the worker believes the session is in.

control_epoch.description: Control epoch the worker is enforcing for this context.

worker_contexts.description: Every browser context the worker holds, for reconciliation (docs/OPERATIONS.md section 9).

contexts.description: The contexts the worker holds. An empty array means the worker holds none, which is a fact rather than an absence of one.

observed_at.description: When the worker enumerated its contexts.

session_allocate.description: Allocation request for one isolated browser context.

organisation_id.description: Owning organisation, carried for defence-in-depth filtering (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3).

project_id.description: Owning project. The worker refuses a project it is not assigned.

agent_session_id.description: Agent session the browser session serves, when one exists.

published_service_id.description: Published service the session may reach (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 10).

service_origin.description: Origin the published service is reachable at. Relative navigation resolves against it, and the worker refuses navigation to any other origin.

service_capability.description: Session-scoped route capability the worker presents to the tunnel gateway on every request to service_origin (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.3). The control plane mints it and the gateway verifies it; the worker only carries it, and never to any other origin.

control_epoch.description: Epoch of the initial control lease.

controller.description: Controller the initial interactive lease is issued to.

limits.description: Limits the worker enforces for this session.

retention_class.description: Retention class recorded on evidence captured in this session.

session_allocated.description: Worker's response to an allocation request.

status.description: Status reached by the allocation, READY on success.

browser_type.description: Browser engine of the allocated context.

browser_version.description: Browser build version, recorded on the session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 12).

viewport.description: Viewport the context was created with.

error.description: Why allocation failed, when status is FAILED.

previous_status.description: Status the session left, included so the event records both sides of the transition (docs/EVENTS.md section 8).

control_epoch.description: Control epoch current at the transition.

current_controller.description: Controller holding the interactive lease at the transition.

session_terminate.description: Instruction to end a session and destroy its ephemeral data.

url.description: Absolute URL or root-relative path resolved against the published service origin.

click_params.description: Input for click. The reference must come from the current snapshot; a stale reference fails rather than clicking whatever now occupies that position.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the reference was issued by.

type_text_params.description: Input for type_text. Secret values MUST NOT be supplied here (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the reference was issued by.

submit.description: Whether to press Enter after typing.

select_option_params.description: Input for select_option. The values name options of the select the reference points at; the schema bounds how many and how long, so a hostile page cannot make one command unbounded.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the reference was issued by.

values.description: Option values to select. More than one is meaningful only on a multiple select.

press_key_params.description: Input for press_key. The key set is closed: a key name is a control instruction to the browser, so it is drawn from a fixed vocabulary rather than passed through.

key.description: Key or modifier combination to press.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the reference was issued by, when the key is directed at one element rather than at the page.

ref.description: Element the key is directed at. Absent means the page has focus.

scroll_params.description: Input for scroll. The distance is bounded, so a scroll is a movement rather than an unbounded loop.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the reference was issued by, when the scroll is inside one element.

ref.description: Element to scroll. Absent means the page scrolls.

resize_params.description: Input for resize. A resize invalidates every outstanding element reference (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4).

wait_params.description: Input for wait. Every condition is bounded; there is no unbounded sleep.

x-requires.detail: a url_matches condition is defined by its pattern alone
a selector condition is defined by its selector alone
a text condition is defined by its text alone
network idleness has no target

snapshot_params.description: Input for snapshot. Both bounds are optional; the session limits supply the defaults.

max_nodes.description: Largest number of elements to describe.

max_bytes.description: Largest rendered snapshot to return before truncation.

full_page.description: Whether to capture beyond the viewport.

persist.description: Whether to upload the capture through the control-plane artefact API. A capture that is not persisted produces no artefact and no evidence.

purpose.description: Why the capture is being taken.

browser_command.description: One browser command. Exactly one parameter object accompanies the command name; the schema forbids the others so a command cannot smuggle an unused parameter set.

timeout_ms.description: Bound on how long the command may run. Exceeding it fails with BROWSER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT rather than waiting indefinitely.

command_error.description: A refused or failed operation, reported with a stable code (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12).

message.description: Operator-facing explanation. Carries no credentials and no unbounded page content.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same command could succeed.

current_epoch.description: Epoch that is actually current, returned with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE so the caller can refresh rather than guess (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 5).

navigation_result.description: Outcome of a navigation. Every field is page-derived and therefore untrusted.

http_status.description: Status of the main document response.

redirected.description: Whether the browser settled on a different URL than requested.

title.description: Document title, truncated to its bound.

element_descriptor.description: One element of a snapshot, addressable by reference until the snapshot is superseded.

ref.description: Reference valid for this snapshot only.

name.description: Accessible name, truncated to its bound.

snapshot_result.description: A bounded accessibility snapshot (docs/MCP_SPEC.md sections 7.4 and 13). Page-derived throughout.

snapshot_id.description: Identity of this snapshot. A reference is accepted only while it is the current snapshot.

viewport.description: Viewport the snapshot was taken at. A resize supersedes it.

truncated.description: Whether the page had more content than the bounds allowed. A truncated snapshot is a summary, never a whole-page dump.

elements.description: Machine-readable form of the same elements.

screenshot_result.description: A screenshot that the control plane has verified and made available (docs/API.md section 15, ADR-0012).

artefact_id.description: Artefact the capture was stored as. Present only once the control plane has verified size and hash.

size_bytes.description: Byte length the control plane verified.

content_type.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

viewport.description: Viewport the capture was taken at.

full_page.description: Whether the capture extends beyond the viewport.

browser_command_result.description: Result of one browser command. The trust rules below are enforced by the generated validators on both sides, so page-derived content cannot be returned without its untrusted label (ADR-0010).

sequence.description: Sequence number of the command this result answers.

control_epoch.description: Epoch current at the worker when the command ran.

trust.description: Trust of the content in this result.

instruction_policy.description: How the receiver must treat that content.

screenshot.description: Verified screenshot artefact. Rendered from page content.

viewport.description: Viewport in force after the command.

x-requires.detail: page-derived content must be labelled untrusted_browser_content (ADR-0010, docs/SECURITY.md section 11)
